questions.q: A parallel beam of light is allowed to fall on a transparent spherical globe of diameter <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>30</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> and refractive index <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn></math>. The distance from the centre of the globe at which beam of light can converge is _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>mm</mi></math>.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For the refraction at the left surface, u=-∞, R=+15 cm.

μ2v-μ1u=μ2-μ1R

⇒1.5v1-1-∞=1.5-1+15

⇒v1=45 cm

For the refraction at the right surface, u=45-30=15 cm, R=-15 cm

μ2v-μ1u=μ2-μ1R

⇒1v2-1.515=1-1.5-15

⇒v2=7.5 cm

Therefore, the distance from the centre where the beam will converge is,

15+7.5=22.5 cm=225 mm

questions.q: A pole is vertically submerged in swimming pool, such that it gives a length of shadow 2.15 m within water when sunlight is incident at an angle of 30° with the surface of water. If swimming pool is filled to a height of 1.5 m, then the height of the pole above the water surface in centimeters is (nw=43) ________.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let angle BAC is θ.

Applying Snell's law at E, we get 1×sin60°=43×sinθ

⇒sinθ=338⇒tanθ=sinθ1-sinθ2=3337

Now, BC=1.5×tanθ=1.28

Then, AB=2.15-BC=0.86 m

Required value, DF=AB tan30°=0.5015 m≈50 cm

δmin=2i-A
A=2i-A

μ=3

t=APv=53×10-23×1083=5×10-10s
So, x=5

questions.q: In an experiment for estimating the value of focal length of converging mirror, image of an object placed at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>40</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> from the pole of the mirror is formed at distance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>120</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> from the pole of the mirror. These distances are measured with a modified scale in which there are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn></math> small divisions in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math>. The value of error in measurement of focal length of the mirror is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>K</mi></mfrac><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>K</mi></math> is ______.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given here, u=-40 cm, v=-120 cm

Using mirror formula, 1v+1u=1f

 -1120-140=1f⇒f=-30 cm

Now, differentiating mirror equation, we get

-1v2dv-1u2du=-1f2df

Also, the least count of scale, dv=du=120 cm

Putting in above equation, 

∴ 120(120)2+120(40)2=df(30)2

On solving, we get

df=132 cm

∴ K=32.

questions.q: Two immiscible liquids of refractive indices 85 and 32 respectively are put in a beaker as shown in the figure. The height of each column is 6 cm. A coin is placed at the bottom of the beaker. For near normal vision, the apparent depth of the coin is α4 cm. The value of α is _______.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the apparent height of the coin when seen through the combination of liquids can be written as

happ=h1μ1+h2μ2   ...1

From equation (1), it follows that

happ=63/2+68/5 cm=4+154 cm=314 cm

Hence, α=31.

questions.q:
The graph between 1u and 1v for a thin convex lens in order to determine its focal length is plotted as shown in the figure. The refractive index of lens is 1.5 and its both the surfaces have same radius of curvatures R. The value of R will be _____ cm.

(Where u= object distance, v= image distance)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For point B, 1u=-0.10 cm-1, 1v=0

∴ Thus, u=-10 cm, v=∞

Using lens formula, 

1f=1v-1u=0--10

⇒f=10 cm

Now, using Lens maker's formula, 

1f=μ-11R1-1R2, where, μ is refractive index of lens.

⇒110 cm=1.5-12R=1R⇒R=10 cm

questions.q:

Taking dispersive powers of crown and flint glass are 0.02 and 0.03 respectively and refractive index for yellow light for these glasses are 1.5 and 1.6 respectively. The refracting angles for crown glass prism will be ________° (in degree)

(Round off to the Nearest Integer)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
ω1=0.02;μ1=1.5; ω2=0.03;μ2=1.6

Achromatic combination

∴ θnet=0

θ1-θ2=0

θ1=θ2

ω1δ1=ω2δ2

and δnet=δ1-δ2=2°

δ1-ω1δ1ω2=2°

δ11-ω1ω2=2°

δ11-23=2°

δ1=6°

δ1=μ1-1A1

6°=1.5-1A1

A1=12°

questions.q: A thin cylindrical rod of length <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> is placed horizontally on the principle axis of a concave mirror of focal length <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math>. The rod is placed in a such a way that mid point of the rod is at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>40</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> from the pole of mirror. The length of the image formed by the mirror will be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is ______.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As per sign conventions, object distance uA=-45 cm, focal length f=-20 cm.

From the mirror formula

1vA+1uA=1f⇒1vA+1-45=1-20⇒vA=-45×(-20)-45-(-20)=-90025⇒vA=-36 cm

And uB=-35 cm

1vB+1uB=1f⇒1vB+1-35=1-20⇒vB=-35×(-20)-35-(-20)=700-15⇒vB=-1403 cm

Now, length of image=vA-vB

=-36+1403 cm

=-108+1403 cm

=323 cm

∴ x=32

questions.q: A thin prism of angle 6° and refractive index for yellow light nY1.5 is combined with another prism of angle 5° and nY=1.55. The combination produces no dispersion. The net average deviation δ produced by the combination is 1x°. The value of x is _____ .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula for deviation due to a thin prism is given by, δ=Aμ-1.

Therefore, for prism 1:

δ1=61.5-1=3°

And for prism 2:

δ2=-51.55-1=-2.75°

⇒δnet=δ1+δ2=3°-2.75°=0.25°=14°

Therefore, x=4.

questions.q: A bi convex lens of focal length <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> is cut in two identical parts along a plane perpendicular to the principal axis. The power of each lens after cut is _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">D</mi></math>.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The focal length of the bi-convex lens f can be calculated as follows:

1f=(μ-1)1R-1-R=2μ-1R   ...1

When the lens is cut into two halves, the focal length f' of each part can be calculated as follows:

1f'=(μ-1)1R-1∞= μ-1R   ...2

Hence, the ratio of the powers for both the lenses can be given by

P'P=1f'1f= ff'=μ-1R2μ-1R=12⇒P'= P2   ...3

Substitute the value of the known parameter into equation (3) to calculate the required power.

P'=10 D2= 5 D

questions.q: A fish rising vertically upward with a uniform velocity of 8 m s–1, observes that a bird is diving vertically downward towards the fish with the velocity of 12 m s–1. If the refractive index of water is 43, then the actual velocity of the diving bird to pick the fish, will be__________m s-1.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let the fish be at a depth x from the surface and let the bird be at height y from the surface. So, with respect to fish

y'=μy+x⇒y'=4y3+x

Differentiating with respect to time,

dy'dt=4dy3dt+dxdt

⇒4y3+dxdt=-12

⇒43·dydt=-12+8=-4

⇒dydt=-3 m s-1

questions.q: A light ray is incident on a glass slab of thickness $4 \sqrt{3} \mathrm{~cm}$ and refractive index $\sqrt{2}$ . The angle of incidence is equal to the critical angle for the glass slab with air. The lateral displacement of ray after passing through glass slab is _____ $\mathrm{cm}$. $\left(\right.$ Given $\left.\sin 15^{\circ}=0.25\right)$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & i=\theta_c \\ & \Rightarrow i=\sin ^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{\mu}\right) \\ & \Rightarrow i=45^{\circ} \end{aligned}$ and according to snell's law $\begin{aligned} & 1 \sin 45^{\circ}=\sqrt{2} \sin \mathrm{r} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{r}=30^{\circ} \end{aligned}$
Lateral displacement $\Delta=\frac{\mathrm{t} \sin (\mathrm{i}-\mathrm{r})}{\cos \mathrm{r}}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \Delta=\frac{4 \sqrt{3} \times \sin 15^{\circ}}{\cos 30^{\circ}} \\ & \Rightarrow \Delta=2 \mathrm{~cm} \end{aligned}$

From lens equation, we can write

⇒f=+10 cm
